intent: Move order notification delivery out of the request path. Notification sending has an independent responsibility and its own failure modes (provider latency, retries, backoff), so it becomes a runnable consumer plus an independently running message broker rather than code inside shop.api. Proposed only: none of this is implemented.

constraints.statement: An order MUST be recorded before the API responds, and customer notification delivery MUST happen outside the request path with independent retries.

alternatives.title: Send the notification synchronously inside shop.api
alternatives.tradeoff: No new containers and no broker to operate. Rejected: provider latency and outages land in the checkout path, a failed send has no retry surface, and a slow provider becomes a checkout incident.

alternatives.title: Outbox table in the product database plus a relay process
alternatives.tradeoff: Strongest guarantee (no lost events even if publishing fails mid-transaction), but it needs a relay worker and a migration on the existing database, so it is a later evolution of this design rather than the first step.

alternatives.title: Independent RabbitMQ broker container plus a notification worker (chosen)
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds two runnable units to operate and monitor. Buys isolation: the API only publishes, delivery retries are independent, and a provider outage drains when the provider returns. Accepted for the first step.

rationale: The responsibility (deliver notifications, retry, back off) is independent of serving customer requests, which is exactly the C4 container criterion: separately runnable, separately deployable, separately failing. The RabbitMQ broker is modeled as a container because it is an independently running system component with persistent message storage; an individual RabbitMQ queue is not independently deployable.
openQuestions: Delivery guarantee: at-least-once is assumed; where notification de-duplication lives is undecided.
Retry cap, backoff schedule and dead-letter handling are not specified by this proposal.
Whether the worker sends directly over SMTP or through a provider API is left open; the model shows a single outbound notification relationship to the customer.

evidence.note: Planned acceptance test for publish-before-respond and independent retry. Nothing is implemented: this path does not exist yet, and completion checks must fail until it does.
